title: Add an opt-in owner-bound selected replay successor
body:
This implements the executable repair handoff from Josie Elliston's PR1959 and Aaron Wang's PR2301: an opt-in successor runs the unchanged selected PR1094 strict verifier, then requires the emitted pooled owner list (all fields, including time) to equal the independently pinned frozen OWNERS list and requires its owner-map digest link to agree. It writes a new `BOUND-REPLAY.json` success receipt only after that conjunction passes.

The new equality is type-sensitive: `false` and `0.0` cannot substitute for integer `0`. The runner also binds the checked template to the actual fresh assembly/owner/invoice/HOSTED receipts, checks the eleven-stage ledger/logs, and preserves existing output. Inherited assertion-based checks stay enabled even when the successor itself is run under `-O` with `PYTHONOPTIMIZE=2`.

Local integration evidence on Python 3.12.3:

- The actual positive completed all 11 unchanged strict stages and the new guard for all 69,120 roles.
- PR2301's equal-width time swap and wrong owner-map digest each still passed all six post-emit stages and all 20 final predicates, then failed the new gate for the intended reason.
- The short registered check passed 15 targeted controls, valid template re-encodings, type-equality counterexamples and output preservation. A Git-free read-only Python 3.14.4 export also passed, with all 22 exported files unchanged.

Start with `research/selected-owner-bound-replay/run_bound.py` and `binding.py`; `README.md` states the contract. `INTEGRATION.json` records the actual full run. The short check explicitly does not claim to run the strict stages:

```sh
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/selected-owner-bound-replay
```

To reproduce the complete integration from pinned archived PR1042 local inputs (about a minute locally):

```sh
python3.12 -I -B research/selected-owner-bound-replay/full_check.py --work /tmp/fresh-owner-bound-integration
```

The dedicated workflow runs that command. Hosted CI is separate from the local receipts. The original PR2301 post-emit runner and final predicates are reused byte-for-byte with paths rebound and explicitly credited, rather than presented as a new independent verifier.

This is an optional successor proposal: frozen sources, the selected record and default entry point are unchanged. Maintainer adoption remains separate. It does not rebuild cold ancestry, establish a physical consumer's correctness from metadata, validate every descriptive template field, prove all-size/precision/analytic obligations, or improve κ. The selected fixture already satisfies the new condition; this closes an acceptance implication.

Base: canonical main `0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2`, priority revision 4. PR2301 head `0b38025ddb2c06f696c54a18f50b0c0228493eab` and main were rechecked before submission. Coordination: [Discussion2347](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2347). Final live text refresh: 564 open PRs (2026-10-15T06:16:58.956719+00:00) and 1078 Discussion records (2026-10-15T06:18:32.685398+00:00), complete pagination and no warnings. This covers text metadata, not arbitrary code diffs.

Gareth Davidson (`bitplane`), with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; no sub-agents or independent human review. The guard idea and diagnosis remain credited to Josie Elliston (Claude Code) and Aaron Wang (opencode). The unchanged construction retains Jeremy Kothe, Hao Yan, Rohan Arun, Douglas Colkitt and the full supplier lineage. PR2158's invoice audit and PR2273's field analysis are complementary existing work. Apache-2.0 and source notices are retained.
